title: In Vesiculo Synthesis of Peptide Membrane Precursors for Autonomous Vesicle Growth
protocol: Prepare and autoclave expression culture flasks.
Autoclave 3 L of LB medium.
For each liter of LB medium, add 25 g of LB powder to 1 L of ultrapure water.
Prepare a starter culture with 100 mL of LB medium.
Add 50 µL of sterile-filtered chloramphenicol solution (25 mg/mL in EtOH) to the starter culture.
Add 50 µL of sterile-filtered carbenicillin solution (100 mg/mL in 50% EtOH and 50% ultrapure water) to the starter culture.
Streak a small amount from a pre-made bacterial stock containing E. coli strain BL21(DE3)pLysS with the pET20b(+) expression vector onto the starter culture.
Incubate the starter culture at 37 °C for 16 h with shaking at 250 rpm.
Pre-warm the expression culture flasks and LB media at 37 °C overnight.
Add 750 mL of LB medium to each pre-warmed expression culture flask.
Add 375 µL of sterile-filtered chloramphenicol stock (25 mg/mL in EtOH) to each flask.
Add 375 µL of sterile-filtered carbenicillin stock (100 mg/mL in 50% EtOH and 50% ultrapure water) to each flask.
Agitate the flasks to distribute the antibiotics evenly.
Take a 2 mL reference sample for OD600 measurement.
Add 7.5 mL of the starting culture to the expression flask and incubate for 1 h at 37 °C with 250 rpm.
Reduce the temperature to 16 °C when the optical density reaches approximately 0.8.
Add 750 µL of 1 M sterile-filtered IPTG into each expression flask.
Incubate the expression flasks at 16 °C for 16 h with 250 rpm.
Pre-weigh the centrifugation flasks to determine the mass of the cell pellet after harvesting.
Centrifuge all bacteria from the expression flasks at 4,000 x g and 4 °C for 20 min.
Pour out the supernatant and blot the centrifuge bottles on a sterile paper towel.
Weigh the centrifugation flasks to calculate the mass of the cell pellet.
Resuspend cells in 15 mL of PBS by pipetting, then centrifuge at 4,000 x g for 20 min at 4 °C.
Pour out the supernatant and blot the centrifuge bottles on a sterile paper towel.
Resuspend the cell pellet in buffer supplemented with lysozyme, PMSF, benzamidine, and DNase I.
Sonicate cells on ice with a sonicator at 8 W for 9 minutes in alternating 10 seconds of sonication and 20 seconds of pausing.
Pause the sample on ice for 9 minutes after the first sonication cycle.
Repeat the sonication step once more following the same procedure as before.
Add 2 mL of 10% (w/v) polyethyleneimine (PEI) per liter of original cell culture for nucleic acid precipitation.
Distribute the treated sample into 2 mL centrifuge tubes.
Incubate the samples at 60 °C for 10 minutes.
Incubate the samples at 4 °C for 10 minutes after the warm incubation.
Centrifuge the solution at 16,000 x g for 10 minutes at 4 °C and collect the supernatant containing the ELP.
Adjust the pH of the supernatant to 2 using phosphoric acid and sodium hydroxide to induce protein aggregation.
Heat the sample to 60 °C and add sodium chloride up to a concentration of 2 M to improve purification yield.
Centrifuge the heated and salted sample at 16,000 x g for 10 minutes at room temperature (RT).
Discard the supernatant after centrifugation.
Re-dissolve the pellet in PBS using half of the initial volume used for precipitation.
Adjust the pH to 7 with phosphoric acid and sodium hydroxide.
Centrifuge the sample again at 16,000 x g for 10 minutes at 4 °C.
Concentrate the ELP solution to 1.1 mM using a centrifugal vacuum concentrator.
Mix 200 µL of concentrated ELP solution with 1,250 µL of a 2:1 chloroform/methanol mixture followed by vortexing.
Add 1.5 g of spherical glass beads (212–300 μm in size) to a 10 mL round bottom flask.
Mix the solution containing ELP and the chloroform/methanol mixture with the glass beads.
Connect the flask to a rotary evaporator, adjust speed to 150 rpm, regulate pressure to -0.2 x 10^5 Pa (-200 mbar), and evaporate liquid at room temperature for approximately 4 min.
Place the round bottom flask into a desiccator for at least 1 h to ensure evaporation of remaining chloroform and methanol.
Mix 100 mg of peptide-covered glass beads with 60 µL of swelling solution, such as PBS.
Incubate this sample at 25 °C for 5 min.
Centrifuge the sample quickly to sediment the glass beads.
Use a pipette to collect the supernatant containing the vesicles.
Clean the lab bench with wipes containing RNase decontamination solution.

Mix ssDNA comprising the T7 promoter and dBroccoli sequence (5 µM) with noncoding strand (5 µM) in nuclease-free water supplemented with RNAPol reaction buffer [40 mM Tris-HCl (pH = 7.9), 6 mM MgCl2, 1 mM dithiothreitol (DTT), and 2 mM spermidine].
Incubate the solution at 90 °C for 5 min.
Decrease temperature to 20 °C over 30 min.
Dissolve 1.26 mg of DFHBI in 5 mL of DMSO to prepare a 1 mM DFHBI solution.
Mix RNAPol reaction buffer with 125 mM KCl, 15 mM MgCl2, 4 mM rNTP, 10 µM DFHBI, 200 nM DNA template, 0.5 U/µL RNase inhibitor murine, and water.
Add 4 U/µL T7 polymerase to the reaction mix immediately before starting the reaction.
Use this reaction mix as the swelling solution in step 2.7.
Incubate at 37 °C for the duration of the experiment, typically 1 hour.
Prepare six overnight cultures with 5 mL of LB medium and 5 μL of sterile-filtered carbenicillin solution.
Incubate the cultures at 37 °C for 16 h with shaking at 250 rpm.
Extract plasmid DNA from bacterial cultures using a mini-prep kit or following an alternative protocol.
Prepare 100 µL of pre-purified plasmid DNA with a concentration ranging from 200–600 ng/µL.
Mix the prepared plasmid DNA with 100 µL of Roti-phenol/chloroform/isoamyl alcohol (pH = 7.5–8.0) in a microcentrifuge tube for phase separation.
Invert the tube up to 6 times and centrifuge for 5 min at 16,000 x g at room temperature.
Add 200 µL of chloroform to the upper phase after centrifugation and invert the tube up to 6 times.
Centrifuge the sample again at 16,000 x g for 5 min at room temperature.
Pipette the supernatant into a separate tube and add 10 µL of 3 M sodium acetate for ethanol precipitation.
Add 1 mL of -80 °C cold ethanol to the supernatant and store the sample at -80 °C for 1 hour.
Centrifuge the sample at 16,000 x g for 15 min at 4 °C.
Decant the supernatant and add 1 mL of -20 °C cold 70% (v/v) ethanol to the pellet.
Centrifuge again at 16,000 x g for 5 min at 4 °C.
Remove liquid from the sample by pipetting carefully without disturbing the DNA pellet.
Store the sample at room temperature for approximately 15 minutes to evaporate remaining ethanol.
Add ultrapure water to adjust the sample concentration to approximately 300 nM, measured by absorption at 260 nm.
Thaw the prepared crude cell extract and reaction buffer on ice.
Add plasmid DNA to 37.5 µL of reaction buffer.
Add 28.7 µL of crude cell extract to the mixture.
Fill the final volume to 58.8 µL with ultrapure water.
Add 1.2 µL of T7 RNA polymerase solution to the reaction mix.
Mix the sample by pipetting up and down.
Incubate the reaction mix at 29 °C for 4–8 h.
Prepare a 20 mM NHS-azide linker solution in DMSO.
Mix 250 µL of ELP solution with PBS and NHS-azide (1.2 mM).
Incubate the mixture for 12 h at room temperature.
Load the sample into a 10 kDa dialysis cassette.
Store the dialyzed sample at 4 °C for 12 h in ultrapure water.
Mix activated ELP (500 µM) with alkyne-conjugated dye (Cy5-alkyne or Cy3-alkyne, 500 µM).
Mix this sample with 1 mM TBTA, 10 mM TCEP, and 10 mM CuSO4.
Incubate at 4 °C for 12 h.
Load the sample in a 10 kDa dialysis cassette.
Store it at 4 °C for 12 h in 1 L of ultrapure water to remove salts and residual alkyne-conjugated dyes.
